final_answer:
PRIVILEGED - WORK PRODUCT. REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
To: Margaret Chen | Re: Saxonbrook markup (Blackmere Tillotson & Hale, Sept. 27, 2024) of Cascade's Aug. 12, 2024 draft Consent Decree, U.S. v. Cascade, No. 3:23-cv-01847-MO (D. Or.)

1. BOTTOM LINE
Do not accept the markup as a basis for negotiation. It (a) moves Cascade's cost to roughly $39.1M against the Board's $32M ceiling, (b) trips all five walk-away triggers in the March 28 strategy memo, (c) contains changes Hale's cover email omits or mischaracterizes, and (d) includes terms DOJ/EPA are very unlikely to lodge. Recommended response: reject the redline as a base; demand a true comparison against our Aug. 12 draft; counter on our paper; and engage EPA/DOJ early (Hale proposes keeping them out, but the government is the check on most of these terms).

2. PROCESS AND INTEGRITY PROBLEMS (resolve first)
- Wrong baseline. The redline's underlying text does not match our draft: different numbering and much shorter text, and it shows as "existing" text our draft lacks (e.g., a Section 11.2(a) cure cross-reference, monthly reporting, 14-day force majeure notice, ORS ch. 174 construction clause). Our draft already required quarterly reports, a 7-day force majeure notice and no cure period. Our no-NRD-credit (para. 57), no-installment (para. 39), no-oversight-cap (para. 51) and reopener (paras. 73-75) text is not in its base. Unmarked changes cannot be ruled out.
- Count. Hale says about 85 edits. The file holds about 183 tracked insertions and 86 deletions in about 125 paragraphs; "conforming edit" comments sit on substantive changes.
- Untracked text. Several changes appear as typed "[ADDED:]/[DELETED:]" text or untracked insertions (6.1(b), 6.3.1, 7.1, 8.1.1, 19.1; 2.3, 2.15, 2.27, 5.1.3, 6.5.2).
- Names/addresses. "Vanguard" appears in the email and redline caption; confirm the correct entity. Hale's redlined notice address differs from his signature block.
- Email vs. redline. First installment: email says 30 days after entry; redline 6.1(b) says 60 days. Cure period: email says 30 days; redline says 15. Reopeners: email mentions only the unknown-conditions reopener; the redline deletes all but non-compliance. The email omits the financial-inability force majeure deletion, 7.2.2, and the 14.2 disclosure duty.

3. CASCADE EXPOSURE (strategy-memo method)
Redline at 70/30: remediation $33,250,000; past costs net $3,355,000 ($4.3M less $945,000); past oversight $574,000; NRD $1,960,000. Total $39,139,000, i.e., $7.14M over the $32M authority, before future oversight ($150-250K/yr) and uncapped indemnity.
Correction to our own memo: its "net" baseline of $32,974,400 double-counts the $1,634,000 reimbursement; $34,608,400 is already net of it. At 62/38 Cascade is already about $2.6M over $32M, and conceding the $680K fees adds about $258K. The Board should hear this before any money concession.

4. SUBSTANTIVE ISSUES: RECOMMENDATIONS
A. Allocation 70/30 (5.1.1, 1.8, 1.14, 2.3, 2.27, 6.4-6.5, 7.2.1) - REJECT; this is walk-away trigger 1 (>67%).
The ROD (Part 1 summary) contradicts Saxonbrook's factual predicates. (i) Methodology expressly weighed waste characterization, toxicity, persistence and fate-and-transport, and rejected duration as a proxy (ROD 6.2). (ii) Saxonbrook's own waste was TCE/PCE, more concentrated per unit volume than Cascade's mixed streams (ROD 6.1-6.3), contrary to the email's "lower toxicity" claim. (iii) Saxonbrook was the sole disposer 2014-2017; the new recital 1.8 ("Cascade operated... the entire period of contamination") is false, and 1.12 ("primary operator") and 1.14 (deleting the 62/38 recital) should be rejected. Cascade's six solo years are already attributed to it; operator status goes to liability category, not mass share. A departure from the EPA-adopted allocation also invites scrutiny at the fairness review. Our ROD copy is unsigned and lacks Appendix E; obtain both. The 62/38 is stated as CVOC mass; metals are attributed mainly to Cascade, so avoid inviting a soil-cost reallocation argument. Granite Bluff (ROR 4.4, 5.3) separately bars Cascade from agreeing to any allocation unsupported by the EPA record without its consent. Offer a technical call on Appendix E only.

B. Payment (6.1, 6.2, 17.1-17.2, 2.15) - COUNTER; non-negotiable in email, but outside our authority as drafted.
Four installments over three years ($3,562,500 each) exceed our ceiling of three installments/18 months. Defects: no interest (we require AFR + 200 bp); Columbia River Commercial Bank is not shown as A- rated; the LOC ($10,687,500) covers installments only; no evergreen or non-renewal draw; EPA alone may draw, after 30 days, and Cascade is not a beneficiary; 6.2.1 adds a 30-day interest holiday on all payments (our memo allows no payment grace); and the force majeure change could excuse financial inability. Counter: up to three installments within 18 months, interest at AFR + 200 bp, 100 percent LOC (principal plus interest) from an A- issuer, evergreen with draw on non-renewal, Cascade co-beneficiary, plus the guarantee.

C. Ridgecrest guarantee deleted (17.1 replaces the guarantee and Exhibit C with a self-representation) - REJECT; must-have. Installments plus no sponsor support is walk-away trigger 3. The 17.1 "representation" is a bare warranty with notice-only covenants (no restriction on dividends, recaps or asset transfers; 25 percent net-asset-drop notice only). Limited liability is no answer; parent guarantees and LOCs are standard financial assurance in EPA settlements. Our $5M cap is about 28 percent of Saxonbrook's share; with client sign-off, trade cap level or form (e.g., guarantee sized to the deferred balance plus financial covenants) for the principle. The LOC alone does not meet our sponsor-support condition.

D. Several-only liability (7.1, 7.2.2, 12) - REJECT as drafted; must-have/walk-away trigger 2.
Legal frame: CERCLA 107(a) liability is joint and several unless the harm is reasonably divisible (Burlington Northern & Santa Fe Ry. v. United States, 556 U.S. 599 (2009)); the ROD itself states joint and several exposure. Cascade is the current owner (107(a)(1)), so EPA keeps J&S reach against it regardless; several-only mainly protects Saxonbrook while stripping Cascade's remedy against a defaulting Saxonbrook. 7.2.2 (no contribution claims against a party that has paid "its share") also bars recovery of cost overruns, and 5.2.2 makes overruns proportional with no cap. Counter: J&S to the United States and State (government-facing); 62/38 inter se with contribution rights preserved; no 7.2.2.

E. Covenant not to sue and reopeners (8.1-8.2) - REJECT.
Redline releases "all claims, known or unknown," under CERCLA, RCRA, CWA and state law, and deletes the unknown-conditions and new-information reopeners. CERCLA 122(f)(6)(A) requires a covenant concerning future liability to except conditions unknown when EPA certifies completion; 122(f)(3) makes a covenant effective only on certification of completion. Our draft keys unknown conditions to ROD signing; conform it to the statute. The government will not agree, and the redline's "Settling Parties fail" trigger is ambiguous on whose default counts.

F. Contribution protection (9.1.1, 2.1, 23.7.1) - REJECT; must-have.
113(f)(2) protects only "a person who has resolved its liability" in an approved settlement, for "matters addressed." Parties cannot confer statutory protection on non-settlors (Ridgecrest, portfolio companies of parents) and cannot enlarge "matters addressed" to "all matters relating to the Facility." It would also bar Granite Bluff's subrogated claims (G) and Cascade's claims against Ridgecrest. Counter: Cascade and Saxonbrook only; delete 23.7.1 carve-out.

G. Insurance (14.2; also 18) - REJECT; walk-away trigger 4.
14.2 forbids Cascade from asserting any insurance claim that could produce subrogation against Saxonbrook, Affiliates or Ridgecrest, and compels delivery of insurer correspondence. Granite Bluff's March 15, 2024 ROR (5.1-5.3) treats exactly that as potential grounds for denial of the $15M coverage, and requires its written consent before any settlement, prompt notice of drafts, and no confidentiality that blocks disclosure to it. The confidentiality clause (18.1-18.3) covers all terms, imposes $250K liquidated damages per breach, and conflicts with public lodging and comment (122(d)(2); 28 C.F.R. 50.7). Reject both; restore our savings clause. Action: send Granite Bluff the redline now (the policy is claims-made and its current term ends Oct. 1, 2024; confirm renewal) and seek consent.

H. Past costs (6.3, 2.19, Ex. E) - COUNTER.
Hale's arithmetic is correct ($3,150,000 x 30% = $945,000). Concede the $680K insurance-coverage fees (not response costs; the workbook itself flags this at D-016 to D-018, which are the lines to be handled carefully). Defend the $470K security: fencing and access control are classic removal measures (CERCLA 101(23)), and the ROD recites them as response measures. Floor: 38% x $3.62M = $1,375,600 (below $1.3M is unacceptable). Reject the new "actually and reasonably incurred" definition (statutory standard is necessary costs consistent with the NCP) and the Exhibit E recital of a "dispute." Before producing more documents, audit weak lines: (i) $310K environmental legal fees: under Key Tronic Corp. v. United States, 511 U.S. 809 (1994), fees for negotiating with EPA or litigating are not response costs (PRP-identification work can be), and D-015/D-029 describe contribution-claim and settlement work; (ii) $544,500 (D-001 to D-003) pre-dates the June 2021 AOC despite para. 21; (iii) D-025 ($100K, Nov. 2023) post-dates the ROD and analyzes pump-and-treat, not the selected remedy; (iv) D-016 is dated Dec. 2023 yet cites the March 2024 ROR; (v) our strategy memo's RI/FS figure ($2.1M) does not match the workbook ($1.285M). Confirm the recovery vehicle: an AOC settlor may be confined to 113(f)(3)(B) (Cooper Indus. v. Aviall, 543 U.S. 157 (2004); United States v. Atlantic Research, 551 U.S. 128 (2007)).

I. NRD credit (6.5, 6.5.2) - REJECT.
Our draft para. 57 bars credits; the ROD (Section 5) says voluntary restoration is creditable only if pre-approved in writing by the trustees (DOI/FWS, NOAA, Oregon) and incorporated in the restoration plan. EPA is not the trustee; Hale's documentation went to EPA. Facts conflict: the email describes 1,200 linear feet of river corridor and 4.3 wetland acres; the redline, 3.5 riparian acres along a "tributary." The credit reduces the joint payment shared 70/30, so Cascade funds $280K of Saxonbrook's credit. Any credit, if trustees approve, must come solely from Saxonbrook's share.

J. Indemnity (13.1-13.3) - REJECT. Mutual uncapped indemnity (our paras. 81-85) becomes uncapped Cascade indemnity (including Saxonbrook "Affiliates" and pre-2003 conditions) against a $5M cap for Saxonbrook, whose 2014-2017 disposal the ROD attributes entirely to it.

K. Early termination (19.1) - REJECT; walk-away trigger 5. "Pay and walk" leaves Cascade, the Site owner, alone for overruns, remedy failure and five-year reviews. Our draft para. 135 provides joint termination.

L. Assignment (3.2, 20.1-20.2) - COUNTER. Duplicative; Cascade (Site owner) needs Saxonbrook and EPA consent, while Saxonbrook may shift obligations to any Affiliate and be released, defeating the LOC. Make it mutual, with EPA consent and no release absent equivalent credit.

M. Arbitration (16.2) - REJECT. It displaces the court retaining exclusive jurisdiction (para. 3) and cannot bind the United States; the final tier stays the District Court.

N. Penalties, force majeure, work takeover, oversight (11, 15, 12, 6.4.3) - COUNTER within limits.
- Penalties: $750/$1,500/$2,500 is below our floor ($1,000/$2,000/$3,500); a 10-15 day cure only for performance defaults, not payments; reject "exclusive remedy" (our para. 91 preserves contempt).
- Force majeure: restore the financial-inability exclusion and para. 107 (no payment relief); reject the regulatory-delay expansion.
- Work takeover: a 90-day cure constrains EPA; offer a 120-125% multiplier (floor 110%) and a shorter cure.
- Oversight cap: $1.2M including $820K past leaves $380K against $1.5M-$3.75M expected; counter at $2-3M future-only with an adjustment mechanism.
- Governing law (21.1): reject; federal law, with Oregon law gap-filling only.

O. Conforming edits. Acceptable: "principal place of business," "Settling Parties," capitalization, typos, 1.1 (adds 113), 10.2.1, 23.3-23.5, 24.2, 10.2.3. Not safe: 1.10 "104(a)" (our recital cites 104 and 122; the ROR says 106(a)); ROD date change; 1.17 (use standard non-admission); 10.1.1 (conflicts with EPA-managed trust performance, para. 59); 22.3 and signatory title (confirm authority); 1.4/Ex. A (no source-concession).

5. NEXT STEPS
1) Obtain Granite Bluff consent and notice. 2) Report corrected exposure and the redline's cost to the Board/GC (Rebecca Park). 3) Call Hale: reject the baseline and request a true comparison, with confirmation that no untracked changes exist. 4) Brief Dr. Lindquist and DOJ on the government-facing items (J&S, reopeners, contribution scope, arbitration, oversight cap, penalties); Hale intends to delay it. 5) Reconcile the workbook. 6) Draft the counter.
